subject: DPA amendment request — subprocessors, customer-managed keys, and signature routing

Subject: DPA redlines + questions on KM responsibilities and signing path

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached are Finlyst's initial redlines to Redwood's standard DPA (Finlyst_DPA_redlines_v1.docx). The two items we need you to confirm quickly are:

- A clear subprocessors exhibit and a commitment to notify 30 days before on-boarding any new subprocessor handling payment or PII.
- Explicit responsibilities around keys (we prefer customer-managed keys / BYOK for production data) and whether Redwood will provide an HSM-backed option or support customer KMS integration.

We'd like to route this through DocuSign for the final execution. Can you confirm who from Redwood will be the signer and whether you can accept our procurement contact on the envelope?

Emily —

Thanks for the note and the redlines. Attaching our initial pass to reflect a 30-day notification on subprocessors and two alternative exhibits for key management (rdw_dpa_with_exhibit_kms_20251113.docx). Quick answers:

- We can accept a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors; we will add a notification clause and maintain a live subprocessor list for customers.
- For keys, we offer two options: our managed keys (HSM-backed) or customer-managed KMS integration (BYOK). The BYOK path requires minimal onboarding (KMS permissions + key usage policy).

Marissa — can you take a look at the redlines for legal language and confirm these proposals are clean from a contract standpoint? Rishi — can you confirm the BYOK integration requirements and whether a short technical exhibit is sufficient?

Best,

Subject: Re: DPA redlines + questions on KM responsibilities and signing path

Karthik / Emily —

I reviewed the attached redlines. High-level suggestions:

1) Subprocessors: Add an express clause that Redwood will maintain a publicly accessible list (or provide on request) and that for subprocessors handling regulated data Redwood will provide SOC2 + encryption-in-transit evidence. We can accept a 30-day notice and a right to object for specific processors with a reasonable remediation window.

2) KMS / Keys: We should avoid specifying internal key custodian names in the DPA. Instead, add an Exhibit (Exhibit K — Key Management) that defines the two supported models: (A) Redwood-managed keys (HSM-backed, rotation policies, access logs), and (B) Customer-managed KMS integration (BYOK) where the customer holds primary key control and Redwood only receives wrapped keys or has API-limited access. Exhibit K should include a minimal set of technical requirements (IAM role with key-use-only permissions, envelope encryption approach).

3) TOMs Exhibit Edits: Encryption at rest (AES-256), TLS 1.2+ for transit, RBAC for key access, and quarterly key rotation for RDW-managed keys. We should add a short paragraph on key rotation auditing and KMS audit logs retained for 12 months.

Emily — if that model works, I'll prepare redline language for Exhibit K and update the main DPA to reference the DocuSign envelope for signature routing.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlyst.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + questions on KM responsibilities and signing path

Marissa — thanks for the clear options. A few follow-ups from Finlyst Security:

- For BYOK, we need confirmation that Redwood will never export plaintext customer keys. The exhibit language should state that Redwood only receives wrapped keys or transient access tokens.
- Can you include an explicit SLA for key revocation and a process for emergency revocation (e.g., 4-hour access cut-off for compromised keys)?
- Subprocessor list: please indicate whether any of Redwood's cloud providers (e.g., GCP/AWS) will be treated as subprocessors for key handling.

We are OK with DocuSign signing. Please prepare a DocuSign envelope with me (Emily Zhao) and our procurement contact as signers on the Finlyst side; let us know who will sign on Redwood's side so we can set routing.

Best,
Emily
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finlyst.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + questions on KM responsibilities and signing path

Emily / Team —

Technical confirmation from SecOps: BYOK integration is supported via customer providing a Cloud KMS key ARN (or equivalent) and granting a service-account principal Encrypt/Decrypt permissions limited to a single key. Key-handling guarantees:

- Redwood will not export plaintext customer keys. We will only receive wrapped key material or call KMS Encrypt/Decrypt APIs on the customer's behalf.
- For RDW-managed keys we use an HSM-backed provider with automatic rotation (90-day rotation window) and KMS audit logs retained for 12 months.
- Emergency revocation: we can support a revocation workflow with a configurable SLA; 4 hours is aggressive but feasible for high-severity incidents if coordinated via a pre-approved emergency contact and auth token exchange.
- Cloud providers: our underlying cloud and managed services (GCP, AWS) are considered subprocessors for infrastructure. For key material, customer-managed KMS keeps key custody outside Redwood; for RDW-managed keys the underlying cloud provider is a subprocessors and covered by our SOC2 controls.

I'll draft a short technical exhibit (kms_integration_diagram.png) and sample wording for the emergency revocation process.

-Rishi
Head of Security — Redwood Inference

Emily —

Thanks — appreciate the quick clarifications. Per Marissa and Rishi's input, we've agreed on the following and I've attached an updated DPA that includes Exhibit K (rdw_dpa_with_exhibit_kms_20251113.docx):

- Subprocessors: 30-day notice, live list, right to object for regulated data processors.
- Key models: Exhibit K with clear BYOK controls (no plaintext export), RDW-managed HSM option, and audit/log retention.
- Emergency revocation: proposed 8-hour SLA by default; 4-hour SLA available as a premium/enterprise option with prior emergency contact setup.

Please confirm the signer on your side for DocuSign (you + procurement). We'll sign on Redwood's side with our Head of Legal (Marissa). If that works, Emily, can you send the DocuSign envelope link and we'll confirm routing?

Next steps: finalize the DPA redline, route in DocuSign, and complete signatures.

Thanks,
Karthik
